reviews.text: "With Thirteen Lives, Ron Howard effectively retells the daring retrieval of a young Thai soccer team from an increasingly deadly cave system."
reviews.author: Jack Walters

reviews.text: Despite the film being based on a true occasion, Thirteen Lives never loses its momentum when it comes to delivering an equally educational and entertaining feature.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: The movie is a prime example of history repeating itself, to show that white saviour narratives are disappointing and take the focus away from the main objective.
reviews.author: Nuha Hassan

reviews.text: You stay for the cinematic underwater sequences and Viggo Mortensen splashing around in a wetsuit, but the rest flounders because of its direction, poor writing, and lack of psychological insight.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: It succeeds in what it’s trying to do, and I definitely felt that it was worth the watch, along with the time I invested into viewing it.
reviews.author: Tyler Strandberg

reviews.text: Told with urgency and sensitivity, the film diligently captures the massive scope of the international rescue effort — with all of its logistical, psychological, and sociopolitical complications — while maintaining a boots-on-the-ground intimacy.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: This is a fact-based account that holds true to everything I remember from the documentary, so it's not playing with the details as much as manipulating the emotions to adhere to more conventional narrative beats.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: The story itself is heart-pounding (and heart-tugging) enough, so Howard allows the actors to stay subtle and nearly fade into the background, never pulling focus for the audience from the dire circumstances of the situation.
reviews.author: Catherine Springer

reviews.text: ...the story was told better by Jimmy Chin and Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi in the 2021 documentary The Rescue, making Howard’s film the equivalent of an English-language remake of a film already done better in another language.
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: I saw someone say that this is like Ron Howard made a Clint Eastwood movie, and yes.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives is certainly watchable and the diving sequences are excruciatingly tense and brilliantly delivered, but if you know the story, there's little else to find here.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: Ron Howard offers a compelling depiction of the 2018 Tham Luang cave rescue...the film pivots from a thrilling depiction of real events, to a moving meditation on the power of community.
reviews.author: Will DiGravio

reviews.text: When Thirteen Lives directs its energies toward illustrating the impossibility of the divers’ mission, the film is solidly compelling.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: This is a really good movie, full of drama and heroism, but I couldn't help comparing it to National Geographic's documentary film depicting the same rescue. This one just isn't quite as good.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: A claustrophobic, suspenseful survival film that knows how to tell its story, Thirteen Lives doesn’t get boring once. The characters have a clear objective, and you will be drawn into the mystery of how they will succeed in their goal.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: Ron Howard plays all the right notes in this retelling of the dramatic rescue of a boys’ football team from a flooded cave-in.
reviews.author: Andy Punter

reviews.text: “Thirteen Lives” is an expertly made hollow shell. It’s like looking at a department store window with nothing in it.
reviews.author: Sarah Manvel

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives is a beautiful depiction of the power of working together for hope.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: The element of breath, the play of water and air, is seamlessly combined into the narrative.
reviews.author: Poorna Banerjee

reviews.text: The 13 lives the title references might as well be sacks of flour, for all the film cares about developing them.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: There’s little in Thirteen Lives that isn’t a matter of public record or treated with more urgency and tension in The Rescue.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives is a riveting account of the cave rescue, and even if you had followed the events closely when they happened, you still wouldn't be prepared for everything that this film reveals.
reviews.author: Gabi Zietsman

reviews.text: The mode is generic, global humanism; Thirteen Lives would sit comfortably on some world news channel playing as background in an over-lit airport lounge.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: Howard manages to keep things tight and engaging, primarily by submerging us right along with the rescue team, engaging us viscerally in the cramped darkness.
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: Nothing short of incredibly gripping, intense, and often nerve-racking, pretty much from start to finish.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Their lives matter, to the point of warranting immense resources to save them (the Thai cave rescue involved 10,000 people and cost $9 million).
reviews.author: Brett McCracken

reviews.text: Mukdeeprom and Howard make Thirteen Lives an entertaining and emotional translation of a major news event that captured the world.
reviews.author: Soham Gadre

reviews.text: A perfect recipe for the sort of unbearable procedural tension that Howard excels at dramatizing.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives is a story about heroism in which no one is a maverick. Everyone is vulnerable and sometimes overwhelmed, and everyone is reluctant to take chances with the boys' lives until it's clear that the alternative is unthinkable.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: Driven by respect for those involved, the story doesn't need to crank up the score or press its characters to evoke emotion or a hammer to remind us that the best of humanity can arise from the worst possible moment... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: At the heart of the new film Thirteen Lives lies a paradox. On the one hand, Ron Howard can be boring and annoying. On the other, caves are really cool, and we all want to see a group of teenagers get rescued from deep in the bowels of one.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: It's a watchable account — Howard knows how to sell every tense moment — but it doesn't have the same dramatic flair as another of the director's films about a real-life escape from jeopardy: Apollo 13.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: All kudos to the huge and impressive production effort of Thirteen Lives. That said, the film does go on and on, defaulting to a rather plodding rhythm in its endeavour to cover every angle, even those well-covered by the world’s media.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Has the best and the worst of this genre: it's spectacular and true to the facts but there are no characters or scenes, just sections of Wikipedia filmed. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Randy Meeks

reviews.text: Director Ron Howard and screenwriter William Nicholson do an excellent, bang-up job of adapting this complex story in to a feature film.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: The acting is understated, but with a good sense of realism showcasing reserved but emotional performances that put me into the characters’ mindsets. Ron Howard captivates and amazes while delivering a touching film filled with nervous optimism.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: Suffocating and suspenseful, Ron Howard's docudrama chronicles an amazing international rescue effort.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Ron Howard is an emotionally driven director, and this is in his wheelhouse, and it is an amazing, captivating story... this does not feel like a Hollywood dramatization at all.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: One of my favorite things about “Thirteen Lives” is Howard’s intense focus on realism. His reliance on authenticity strips the film of artifice and keeps melodrama at a bare minimum. For that reason its tension feels organic and its emotions are earned.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Though the true story is still filled with tense life-or-death situations and nail-biting decision making, Howard's feature version is strangely lacking in personality.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: Viewers unversed in the account and unfamiliar with the two earlier screen versions might enjoy Thirteen Lives, but for everyone else, there’s not much new here beyond the appeal of Hollywood production values and movie stars.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Howard is the supreme master of really good movies where you know the ending.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: Like he did in “Apollo 13,” Howard creates a suspenseful narrative out of a historical account where we know the outcome, but he keeps us enthralled.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: It does have a pretty lean, anti-sensational journalistic vibe, a lot of hand-held cinematography as the camera shoves its way into spaces to watch intently as characters figure out what to do.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Howard cleverly structures the movie as a straightforward procedural that does not require any juicing of the script or showy acting whatsoever.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: I think it will be a better movie 20 years from now when the details of the real events aren’t still fresh, but by God, it gets the job done.
reviews.author: Dustin Rowles

reviews.text: Howard and crew achieve a nearly ideal balance between exposition and story with this film. They seem to have a radar for how to make esoteric information accessible. As with Apollo 13, the technical information is never dumbed down.
reviews.author: Dan Lybarger

reviews.text: Keeps your attention even if you already know the outcome.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Ron Howard’s film is a restrained but still gripping retelling, led by a commitment to realism and a deep respect for all those involved.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: After nearly a decade of floundering, director Ron Howard has seemingly just casually dropped off one of his best efforts.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: It is cinematographer Sayombhu Mukdeeprom’s breathtaking, scuba footage, by turns, intensely claustrophobic, repeatedly confusing, and always dangerous.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives may be the most engrossing, satisfying film of Ron Howard’s career.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: On the downside, it’s too long, it’s a bit flat and linear, and you don’t really get a feel for any of the characters... That said, the basic raw material is so strong that it’s hard not to become involved in the story.
reviews.author: James Delingpole

reviews.text: For all its scuba-diving wizardry, the film’s title is the extent of the detail you’ll get about the kids at its center.
reviews.author: Sara Stewart

reviews.text: Avoiding excessively heightened melodrama, Thirteen Lives doesn’t substitute it with much that one couldn’t already find in the copious amount of available coverage of the real-life incident.
reviews.author: Pat Brown

reviews.text: Howard’s film deftly captures the tension of the situation, skirting the disaster-porn traps that befall other based on a true story films, and uplifts the very encouraging story of the human spirit, even if it means adjusting the details in the process.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Howard manages to eke out a compelling—albeit shallow—action flick.
reviews.author: Aurora Amidon

reviews.text: This film makes us feel we are there. And so we really do care!
reviews.author: Betty Jo Tucker

reviews.text: Howard’s deep skill and empathy raise the film from an ‘adventure action’ film to a think piece, a true and harrowing but measured interpretation.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: This proves that a well-executed traditional narrative is still extremely effective, it traps us with its protagonists through their circumstances and moves us when the situation calls for it. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: Ron Howard delivers a solid and gripping drama based on truly heroic real events. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Despite already knowing the outcome, this film still managed to keep me on the edge of my seat. It's a great example of empathetic filmmaking with excellent performances all around. Most importantly, it doesn’t suffer from the white-savior complex.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: A simple and frank study of the few (almost) anonymous superheroes and the frailty of life, Thirteen Lives is just one of the possible movie adaptations that could've been made about the Tham Luang cave rescue. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text: Howard's film builds up tension aided by Benjamin Wallfisch's music, never strident, and at times the absence of it serves the film well. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: His latest directorial effort in Thirteen Lives proves that [Ron] Howard still has what it takes to make a solid movie based on a true story, which is easily his best one since Rush in 2013.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: “Thirteen Lives” is not an exhibition of spectacle in scale or execution. It neither skirts over details too quickly nor goes too deep into technical aspects, arming the audience with enough to know how much is at stake and why.
reviews.author: Simon Thompson

reviews.text: The movie's a bit of a harrowing ordeal at times, especially for those of us with a claustrophobic streak, but it's just about impossible not to invest in it emotionally.
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: I'm not sure that Thirteen Lives really needed to be helmed by an Oscar winning director, however, I am sure that the film benefits greatly from being helmed by one of contemporary cinema's greatest optimists in Ron Howard.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives is a powerful true story that is told in a compelling way. Howard’s focus on the underwater scenes is evident, and the sound design is fantastic. It may be a bit overlong, but the experience is emotional.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Even though we know the incredible outcome and a true to fact documentary (The Rescue) on the incident came out last year, Thirteen Lives is still appropriately tense and thrilling despite being told with Hollywood theatrics. Only Ron Howard can do that.
reviews.author: T.J. Callahan

reviews.text: A great true story doesn’t need too many flourishes, and a steady director like Howard is just what’s needed to make Thirteen Lives a compelling piece of cinema.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: The film focuses solely on the brains of the men involved in the operation. As a result, it neglects the most cinematic of human possessions — the heart.
reviews.author: Gayle Sequeira

reviews.text: Quality wise, “Thirteen Lives” falls somewhere above the middle of the pack in Howard’s filmography. It’s not “Apollo 13” but it is his best live-action effort in the last decade. That’s nothing to sneeze at.
reviews.author: Michael Clark

reviews.text: It fails to inspire with the grandeur such a story deserves, nor to convey the tireless perseverance and generosity of the heroes involved. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: It lacked suspense, tautness, and felt kind of dry.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: Deliberately paced and gripping, this tells a pragmatic story without the Hollywood flash.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: The subterraneous scenes are brilliantly handled, almost unbearably claustrophobic, and Mortensen and Farrell are quite the vaudeville double act.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: It’s still a fine piece of work, though at just under two and a half hours it runs a little long.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Director Ron Howard, his cinematographer Sayombhu Mukdeeprom, and his sound designer Michael Fentum convey the oppressively claustrophobic conditions in these underwater sequences...
reviews.author: Prahlad Srihari

reviews.text: Mr. Howard deploys exciting music, engineers suspenseful twists and delivers emotionally wrenching scenes that build to a grand payoff. In his fifth decade as a filmmaker, he might be Hollywood’s most enthusiastic purveyor of uplifting goodness.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Howard tells a story about sheer, unrelenting competence with precisely that.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: The filmmaking itself ultimately comes off more procedural than soaring, but also refreshingly stripped of the cloying or sentimental: a remarkable story torn from true life, and faithfully told.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Though Howard’s late arrival at the rescue party has lessened the legacy and relevance of his film, Thirteen Lives is likely the best of the multiple versions, allowing the audience to feel the crisis in a way few directors can.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: 13 must be Ron Howard's lucky number. This true story of the 2018 rescue of the Thai soccer team is a gripping, suspenseful ride. This might be Howard's best film since Apollo 13.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Long but not overlong at 147 minutes, “Thirteen Lives” is sober and gripping, with an interest in the drama of men and women at work that wouldn’t be out of place in a Howard Hawks movie.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Instead of a thrilling piece of narrative storytelling, Howard’s grounded filmmaking approach relegates “Thirteen Lives” to a good companion piece to Nat Geo’s “The Rescue.”
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Simultaneously a thriller and a rescue-diver procedural, one that’s full of tension for nearly its entire 140-minute running time. It’s also the best feature film Ron Howard has made in nearly a decade.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Despite the issues with the rights, Howard succeeds in conveying the Herculean task of the compelling Tham Luang cave rescue.
reviews.author: Therese Lacson

reviews.text: A properly entertaining drama that gets across the technical details with great efficiency. A good job of work by a reliable Hollywood professional.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: The heart of the movie is the discussions among the divers and, even more, the scenes in the caves. Simply as a technical achievement, the underground and underwater filming is highly impressive.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: The unquenchable hope, the remarkable resilience, and the cooperation of all involved  are a story of uplift and the best that humanity has to offer.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: For those who are unaware of what efforts were actually taken, this is going to be a thrilling spectacle that shocks. For those who are aware, this is a rather passable cinematic outing that easily can be skipped.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives tells a story of complex processes with admirable simplicity and no shortage of humanity.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Ron Howard sheds Hollywood hysterics in a pared-down, empowering film about humanity coming together for a common goal. Thirteen Lives is a balm for these torrid times.
reviews.author: Rohan Naahar

reviews.text: Although it’s expertly made, the movie lacks dramatic tension because it focuses on the story of the rescuers and little attention is paid to the perspective of the trapped boys.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: I expect most audiences to be overcome with inspiration and exhilaration after watching Thirteen Lives. The excellent acting and careful storytelling make the length truly worth the watch.
reviews.author: Alyshia Kelly

reviews.text: Perhaps a little on the long side, but the rescue itself is staged with real tension, and the stirring finale is expertly judged.
reviews.author: Patrick Cremona

reviews.text: Howard has a lot of story to tell and there are few directors in Hollywood with such control of classical technique. Even if you’ve seen the excellent documentary from last year, the film is gripping.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: As a standalone work, the film is solid no-frills based-on-a-true-story drama from Hollywood’s top metteur en scène. If The Rescue was a daring-do by documentary adventurers, Thirteen Lives is dad cinema in top form.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: William Nicholson and Howard take the time to create authentic Thai characters and not turn this into another white savior story.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: For those uninitiated to the harrowing true story – and, I learned, there are some – you get all of the tension, dangers and trials these brave men endured to save all 13 lives.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: A rock-solid example of old-fashioned Hollywood craftsmanship, the kind of thing that used to pack people into movie theaters.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: The cinematographer Sayombhu Mukdeeprom uses rain the way film noir uses shadows, creating a gloom that washes over the cast.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Real-life heroes don't come with capes or slow-motion entrances, and neither do the brave men in Howard's grounded, solid telling.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: “Thirteen Lives” could have easily fallen in the trappings of melodrama, but Howard plays the events straight which leaves the movie with a sense of authenticity.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Like its protagonists, it isn’t flashy but is all business. It gets the job done with a minimum of histrionics, yet a mountain of suspense.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives does away with most of the big rescue movie tropes. The drama here is in the effectiveness of the mission’s careful planning and its bold execution.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Perhaps Howard was being trepidatious about returning to this style of filmmaking, though, because Thirteen Lives is more of a technical success than a creative or emotional one.
reviews.author: Glenn Dunks

reviews.text: [An] expertly made, compelling, and satisfyingly multifaceted telling of the uplifting event by Ron Howard.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: A suspenseful, compassionate and disciplined film.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: Howard was always going to have trouble topping The Rescue’s heady mix of real-life footage and cleverly constructed re-enactments, but there’s no doubting this is a compelling tale, sensitively and smartly designed for maximum engrossment.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Ron Howard directs this outstanding humanist epic about the real-life rescue of a Thailand soccer team starring Colin Farrell, Viggo Mortensen and Joel Edgerton.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: There are pockets of diffusive heroes everywhere and that means a lack of tautness or through-line. Neither the divers nor kids, government officials nor families and volunteers really come into focus, staying as murky as the miles of submerged cave.
reviews.author: Mark Kennedy

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives, a fictional representation of the cave rescue operation, is refreshing in the way how anti-spectacle it is. [Ron] Howard doesn't mine the trauma of the young boys for an adrenaline boost for his leading men...
reviews.author: Tatsam Mukherjee

reviews.text: Superheroes may dominate kids' entertainment, but director Ron Howard superbly showcases real heroes who pull off an extraordinary feat to save lives.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: Director Ron Howard is similarly painstaking in depicting the affair; undoubtedly, the film is a technical achievement. He’s so painstaking, in fact, that the film grows tiresome almost immediately.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives is well-constructed, well-directed, and well-acted. Technically speaking, it's impressive how much it really gets across to the audience. A tighter focus would have given it a better emotional throughline...
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: From the start, Thirteen Lives grips you and doesn't let go.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: As scripted, documentary-style fact-based dramas go, it doesn’t get much better than this.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: Howard creates a tightly paced nail-biter with Thirteen Lives. While its nonstop dramatic tension will keep one on edge throughout, the absence of emotional engagement alongside the derivative ending will likely leave some feeling short-changed.
reviews.author: Andrew Murray

reviews.text: Despite the fact that we all know the outcome, and that it’s the third film in as many years to tell the story, Ron Howard’s account of the drama is compulsively watchable and breathlessly tense.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: I’m glad I saw both films, though ‘The Rescue’ is by far the more essential, and ‘Thirteen Lives’ covers a lot of the same ground.
reviews.author: Steven D. Greydanus

reviews.text: Ron Howard’s stirring film about the 2018 Tham Luang cave rescue boasts a strong cast—led by Viggo Mortensen, Colin Farrell, and Joel Edgerton—and sharp, proficient style.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: Farrell and Mortensen effortlessly click together...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: This is a moving film. The title, Thirteen Lives, goes to the still-beating heart of it.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives is highly watchable, featuring some terrific performances, and perhaps a better grasp of some of the ethical questions surrounding this rescue.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: The film is a welcome return to form for Howard, containing all the makings of a competently crafted crowd-pleasing drama.
reviews.author: Sam Rosenberg

reviews.text: Howard also resists the urge to emphasize the true story’s white saviour element.
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: The effort to rescue 12 boys and their soccer coach from a flooded cave in Thailand that captured the world’s attention in 2018 is rivetingly depicted in one of the best directorial efforts by prolific filmmaker Ron Howard.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Howard has filled his cast with the kind of unfussy, selfless actors who will happily chew over the minute details of their characters instead of conjuring any kind of grandeur about themselves. A story this extraordinary can tell itself, really.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: ... A profoundly passionless exploration of a mission that is readymade for thrills, spills and handkerchiefs but has been clearly neutered by Team Hollywood’s primal fear of treading into “White Saviour” territory.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Legions of saviors, including Thai Navy SEALS, demonstrate the Right Stuff in scenes that are simultaneously spooky, poignant and thrilling.
reviews.author: Michael Sragow

reviews.text: To the credit of Howard and his screenwriter, William Nicholson, the Hollywood hokum factor in Thirteen Lives is fairly low. They understand that this story doesn’t need juicing; it just needs to be well told.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: When not in the caves with the divers, Howard is content to tell this story in such a drab, ho-hum, overly respectful fashion that it starts to drag.
reviews.author: Odie Henderson

reviews.text: Thrilling to watch at every moment and a cinematic triumph.
reviews.author: Michael Medved

reviews.text: Ron Howard crafts an absorbing account of a rescue operation that captivated the world. Thirteen Lives has superb technical traits that illustrate the immense difficulty of an unparalleled situation.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives is unbelievably inspirational, nail biting story of what happens when sacrifice, love and support comes from the unlikeliest of places providing the most satisfying results with stunning direction and cinematography leaving you breathless
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: Luckily, we have the benefit of being able to read the future even as we watch Thirteen Lives, and that leaves us free to enjoy Howard’s crackerjack storytelling skills, not to mention the picture’s bracing, casually heroic lead performances.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Maybe the producers know that viewers looking for a more contemplative retelling can find that version elsewhere. For whatever reason, Howard lets his film’s leads remain as murky as the rising floodwaters.
reviews.author: Selina Lee

reviews.text: Last-minute Hollywood-ness doesn't take down the viewing experience, which retains earned emotion, refreshingly understated performances, and a high level of claustrophobia, giving Howard one of his best films in recent memory.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: “Thirteen Lives” is a gripping and suspenseful experience. It'll have you holding your breath until the very end.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: We already know the ending but the drama as rescuers risk killing the boys to save their lives will have you gasping for breath.
reviews.author: Mike Ridley

reviews.text: At almost two-and-a-half hours, the film itself feels like a slog. Still, just like the floodwater, the tension slowly rises, and sporadically engulfs us.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Howard’s film grips but, if you want to understand the pressures endured by these divers, the documentary The Rescue is a tense and deeper take on the same tale.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: “Thirteen Lives” deserves to be seen.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: “Thirteen Lives” may be a vivid rescue procedural first and foremost, but it’s also a testament to the guardian spirit possible in any of us.
reviews.author: Robert Abele

reviews.text: We watch the skilled rescuers problem-solve and come up with innovative solutions to the unimaginable. But once we see them make the trip a handful of times, the overlong film settles into a much too comfortable groove.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: ... manages to be inspirational without being overly sentimental and technical without being cold.
reviews.author: Tyler Smith

reviews.text: An exhilarating, gripping and powerful emotional experience. It also has just the right balance of Truth and Spectacle.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: Howard’s most satisfying film since the early 2000s.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives does a superb job recreating the claustrophobic conditions inside the labyrinth-like cave.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: While certain elements feel underdeveloped, ﻿Thirteen Lives﻿ is an affecting look at one of the most incredible events of the past decade.
reviews.author: Rachel LaBonte

reviews.text: Much like he did with Apollo 13, Ron Howard takes an outsized moment in history, the 2018 Thai soccer team rescue, and reshapes it into an intimate event that allows the audience to experience the intensity and stakes of the ordeal.
reviews.author: Tara Bennett

reviews.text: If Thirteen Lives can sometimes seem just a fraction too low-key, you are left grateful for such sound judgment: the wisdom of skilled film-makers in a tight situation.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: Despite [Ron] Howard bringing his typically high level of craftsmanship to the proceedings, Thirteen Lives rarely feels like essential viewing,
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: Taking a journalistic approach that’s similar to its predecessor, Howard’s film winds up as a rote retread, transitioning from headline news to big-screen snooze.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: Whatever its limitations, Thirteen Lives still has an amazing story to tell.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: just how could [Howard] make a story which had already been told so expertly in a 2021 documentary worthwhile a mere year later?  The answer is surprisingly well, largely due to a well cast ensemble and production crew committed to realism.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Do I prefer the documentary? Absolutely. Is this a solid inspirational film? Yes it is.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Ron Howard has adapted the true story that conveys how dangerous the mission was and how civilians and the military can come together for the common good.
reviews.author: John Nguyen

reviews.text: Ron Howard continues to be a filmmaker who literally shows he can do anything, and with a combination of talented Western and Thai actors, Thirteen Lives is one of his best narrative films in many years.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives is much more subdued, even restrained... Howard knows how to make a tale thrilling even when you already know how the story ends.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: For a film about such dramatic events, this is dull and pointless. It’s too long as well as lacking focus, the weight of the events isn’t felt
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: A well-crafted if somewhat predictable docudrama about the 2018 Thai cave rescue stars Viggo Mortensen and Colin Farrell and kicks into gear in its second half, when the triumphant rescue is mingled with a sense of nightmarish dread.
reviews.author: Liam Lacey

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives is not a bad movie, just a somewhat unnecessary one, given Ron Howard has no interest in differentiating from The Rescue with this incredible true story that does deserve to be told in more ways than one
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: There is a tremendous grandeur to this story, and this film adaptation could have easily gone for big stars and forgotten the intimate, cooperative narrative of the real-life events.
reviews.author: Abe Friedtanzer

reviews.text: Cutting against the grain of exploitative Hollywood translations, Howard humbly steps out of the way to let the power of the story speak for itself, while injecting just enough tension to keep it a white-knuckle affair.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: For its first half, Thirteen Lives feels like it is treading water, waiting for its big final act. Thankfully, the second half is a riveting depiction of a daring, foolhardy, inspired rescue.
reviews.author: Ian Freer

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives is a bland, scripted counterpart to the superior documentary The Rescue, presented mainly from the perspectives of the rescuers. It gives the bare minimum of screen time to the Thai people who suffered the most during this crisis.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Thirteen Lives showcases what true heroism looks like when the odds seemed impossible for a rescue.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: It’s the third film in four years based on the seemingly impossible rescue in Thailand in 2018, and although it’s extremely competent, it fails to add a new perspective to the story or a distinctive approach to its telling.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: The story it tells is incredible enough to survive any deficiencies in the telling, and Howard is far too competent a filmmaker to interfere with its basic power. Still, Thirteen Lives often seems engrossing in spite of itself.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: It’s a fulsome film, both emotionally and as a production.
reviews.author: Todd McCarthy

reviews.text: Two and a half very long hours that rehash much of the details and revelations already covered in Jimmy Chin and Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi’s excellent documentary, The Rescue.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Howard’s film is a paean to the courage and canniness of the seasoned non-professional: subterranean heroism has never looked so down-to-earth.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Even now, years later, that level of teamwork is breathtaking, and Howard’s choice to chronicle those efforts gives Thirteen Lives its own kind of staying power.
reviews.author: Lovia Gyarkye

reviews.text: Howard conveys the claustrophobia and danger of the cave system – although, for a non-caver like me, the question of why anyone should want to cave dive in the first place remains unanswered.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: It never quite does justice to the claustrophobic terror of these traumatic events.
reviews.author: Trevor Johnston

reviews.text: A Visually Accomplished Ticking-Clock Thriller With Nuanced Central Performances.
reviews.author: Jeff Ewing

reviews.text: It's not one of Ron Howard's worst films, but given the subject matter and everything he had to work with, it should've been one of his very best.
reviews.author: Matt Neglia

reviews.text: … a masterful piece of humanistic cinema that also doubles as a heart-stopping adventure …
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

synopsis: Thirteen Lives recounts the incredible true story of the tremendous global effort to rescue a Thai soccer team who become trapped in the Tham Luang cave during an unexpected rainstorm. Faced with insurmountable odds, a team of the world's most skilled and experienced divers -- uniquely able to navigate the maze of flooded, narrow cave tunnels -- join with Thai forces and more than 10,000 volunteers to attempt a harrowing rescue of the twelve boys and their coach. With impossibly high stakes and the entire world watching, the group embarks on their most challenging dive yet, showcasing the limitlessness of the human spirit in the process.
